claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses unconditionally into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression, but AndAlso/OrElse do not propagate NULL under three-valued logic, so an operand under a logical connective is wrongly treated as null-propagating and DropNotNullChecks deletes the IS NOT NULL guard that was the only thing producing null.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` operands as null-propagating, so a live `IS NOT NULL` guard is deleted … it recurses into **both operands of every `SqlBinaryExpression`**, unconditionally … an operand buried under an `AndAlso`/`OrElse` lands in `nullPropagatedOperands` even though its NULL-ness does **not** force the result to NULL.

claim: Boolean-valued when-clause results are not null-propagating once SQL Server's SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor.ConvertToValue materializes the predicate as CASE WHEN p THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (UNKNOWN becomes false, never NULL), so deleting the outer CASE ... ELSE NULL END makes the projection unable to ever yield null.
raw: #2 🟠 High: boolean-valued results are not null-propagating in a value position; the enclosing `CASE` is the only thing producing NULL … **UNKNOWN maps to `0` (false), never to NULL.** The outer `CASE WHEN X IS NOT NULL … ELSE NULL END` was the *only* construct carrying NULL out to the `bool?` projection. The new optimization deletes it, and nothing downstream restores it.

claim: A SqlBinaryExpression carrying Coalesce would also be recursed into and COALESCE does not propagate NULL, but the scenario collapsed on reachability because SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce emits a SqlFunctionExpression with argumentsPropagateNullability [false, false].
raw: - **`Coalesce` as a `SqlBinaryExpression`.** `SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator` permits it and `COALESCE(a,b)` is emphatically not null-propagating, so the line 626 recursion would be unsound. Collapsed on reachability: `RelationalSqlTranslatingExpressionVisitor` routes every `Coalesce` to `SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce`, which builds a `SqlFunctionExpression`

claim: Recursion into And/Or/ExclusiveOr operands was considered but is sound, because boolean And/Or are converted to AndAlso/OrElse earlier and only integer bitwise ops (which propagate NULL) arrive here.
raw: - **`SqlBinaryExpression { And, Or, ExclusiveOr }`.** Boolean `And`/`Or` are converted to `AndAlso`/`OrElse` before reaching here, so these only arrive as integer bitwise ops, which do propagate NULL. Sound.

claim: String Add was considered as an unsound recursion target but AddNullConcatenationProtection wraps nullable operands in COALESCE(x, '') whose arguments do not propagate nullability, so the operand is correctly not collected.
raw: - **String `Add`.** `AddNullConcatenationProtection` wraps nullable operands in `COALESCE(x, '')`, whose `argumentsPropagateNullability` is `[false, false]`, so the wrapped operand is correctly *not* collected. The `Is_not_null_optimizes_binary_op_with_partial_checks` baseline is correct.

claim: HashSet<SqlExpression> / expression-identity equality was considered as a failure mode but all relevant expression types override Equals/GetHashCode structurally, and a mismatch could only cause a missed optimization, never an unsound one.
raw: - **`HashSet<SqlExpression>` equality.** `ColumnExpression`, `SqlBinaryExpression` and `SqlUnaryExpression` all override `Equals`/`GetHashCode` structurally; a mismatch could only cause a *missed* optimization, never an unsound one. … **quick-reviewer / broad-reviewer** — both dismissed expression-identity and `HashSet` equality concerns on the same (correct) reasoning

claim: The nullable out-parameter left set after the early return clause.Result was considered but elseResult is a null constant so nullable is already true, and over-reporting nullability is conservative.
raw: - **`nullable` out-parameter after the early `return clause.Result`.** `elseResult` is a null constant, so `nullable` is already `true` at that point. Over-reporting nullability is conservative.

claim: Loss of type mapping or collation when returning clause.Result directly was considered but CaseExpression derives Type/TypeMapping from whenClauses[0].Result and ApplyTypeMappingOnCase pushes the mapping into each result, so both are preserved.
raw: - **Type mapping / collation loss on `return clause.Result`.** `CaseExpression`'s constructor derives `Type` and `TypeMapping` from `whenClauses[0].Result`, and `ApplyTypeMappingOnCase` pushes the mapping down into each result, so both are preserved.

claim: A mismatch between ArgumentsPropagateNullability and Arguments counts in the indexed loop was considered but the SqlFunctionExpression constructor throws InconsistentNumberOfArguments unless the counts match, so the loop cannot go out of range.
raw: - **`ArgumentsPropagateNullability` / `Arguments` count mismatch** at lines 640-645. The `SqlFunctionExpression` constructor throws `InconsistentNumberOfArguments` unless the counts match, so the indexed loop cannot go out of range.

claim: The func.Instance! null-forgiving dereference could throw a NullReferenceException, but only for constructor argument combinations no in-tree caller produces; recorded as pre-existing and out of reach.
raw: - **`func.Instance!` NRE** at line 635, and `func.ArgumentsPropagateNullability` NRE when `niladic: false, arguments: null`. Both require constructor argument combinations no in-tree caller produces. Recorded `pre-existing, out of reach`.

claim: func.ArgumentsPropagateNullability could throw a NullReferenceException when a function is constructed with niladic false and null arguments, but no in-tree caller produces that combination; recorded as pre-existing and out of reach.
raw: - **`func.Instance!` NRE** at line 635, and `func.ArgumentsPropagateNullability` NRE when `niladic: false, arguments: null`. Both require constructor argument combinations no in-tree caller produces. Recorded `pre-existing, out of reach`.

claim: The new tests' seed data and shape were checked for inadequacy but the NullSemanticsData seed is a 3x3x3 matrix that does exercise the needed NULL combinations and the public virtual + provider-override pattern matches siblings, so nothing was flagged.

Verified the `NullSemanticsData` seed is a 3×3×3 matrix (27 rows) over `[0, 1, null]` / `["Foo", "Bar", null]`, which does exercise the NULL combinations the five new tests need; the `public virtual` + provider-override pattern matches siblings in the same file

raw: and the updated GearsOfWar baselines still assert meaningful behavior.

claim: No new test or updated baseline covers a boolean-typed when-clause result (all use value-typed results), which is why the suite stays green despite finding #2 — explicitly not reportable as a finding under reach=narrow.
raw: Worth noting against finding #2: every one of the five new tests and every updated baseline in this changeset uses a **value-typed** result. The boolean-result shape is not covered anywhere in the changeset, which is why the test suite is green despite the defect. Under `reach=narrow` a coverage gap is not reportable as a finding, but it explains the absence of a failing test.

raw: **The test projects do not compile under the only installed SDK.** `dotnet test test/EFCore.Sqlite.FunctionalTests` fails with `CS0023` / `CS8604` in `test/EFCore.Specification.Tests/CustomConvertersTestBase.cs:1202` … This is a **pre-existing toolchain mismatch**, not caused by this change … Not reported as a finding (out of reach, and not introduced here).
